papers.title: How 'Real' is Your Real-Time Simultaneous Speech-to-Text Translation System?
papers.summary: Survey/critique arguing most SimulST research over-simplifies (pre-segmented speech, inconsistent terminology) and should adopt computation-aware latency, unbounded-speech evaluation, and SimulEval-based joint quality-latency curves.
key_findings: SimulEval is the dominant eval framework (61/110 papers surveyed)
computation-aware latency (incl. real compute time / RTF) is essential for honest benchmarking
cascade vs end-to-end: end-to-end trends better for simultaneous settings due to cascades accumulating ASR+MT delay and error propagation

papers.title: Re-Translation Strategies for Long Form, Simultaneous, Spoken Language Translation / Re-translation versus Streaming for Simultaneous Translation
papers.summary: Shows re-translation (re-translate the whole growing source on every ASR update) can match or beat streaming systems on final quality, but causes caption flicker; proposes masking (truncate last few words) and biasing (bias decoding toward the previous output) to nearly eliminate erasure while preserving quality.
key_findings: re-translation alone can be 'as good or better than SOTA streaming systems, even under constraints allowing very few revisions'
directly describes this repo's current behavior: interim ASR results are re-translated (pipeline.py is_final=False path), i.e. re-translation without masking/biasing

papers.title: Turning Whisper into Real-Time Transcription System
papers.summary: LocalAgreement-n policy: only commit the longest common prefix agreed across n consecutive hypotheses from overlapping buffers. CUNI-KIT found n=2 most effective.
key_findings: LocalAgreement-2 is a simple, rule-based stability policy applicable to any incremental hypothesis stream, including our Deepgram interim-result -> LLM-translation stream

papers.title: Normalized erasure metric (definition)
papers.summary: Defines normalized erasure (NE): tokens deleted from the previous partial's suffix to produce the next partial (via longest common prefix), normalized by output length. NE=0 means no displayed token was ever revised.
key_findings: this repo currently logs chrF/latency/glossary but has zero instrumentation for revision/flicker -- direct, cheap, high-value gap to close first

papers.title: AlignAtt4LLM: Fast AlignAtt for Decoder-Only LLMs at IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation Task
papers.authors: unread -- found via WebSearch 2026-09-08, extracted via WebSearch 2026-09-08 (WebFetch blocked on arxiv.org in this environment, see note below)
papers.summary: A synchronous cascade for En->De/It/Zh: Qwen3-ASR with forced alignment produces an incrementally updated source transcript, and Gemma-4 E4B-it translates that prefix under an MT-side AlignAtt policy -- the first application of AlignAtt (attention-based emit-decision) to a decoder-only LLM, recovered despite the LLM lacking the encoder-decoder cross-attention earlier AlignAtt systems relied on, via (1) an explicit source span in the prompt, (2) offline-selected translation-specific alignment heads, (3) selective qk-fast replay of the draft-to-source attention block, and (4) runtime query/key capture that reproduces model outputs bit-identically. Outperforms IWSLT2026 baselines for En->De/It in both low-latency (~2s) and high-latency (<4s) regimes.
key_findings: AlignAtt's commit rule is fundamentally different from LocalAgreement-2: it inspects the LLM's own internal attention weights (which source tokens the next target token is attending to) to decide when enough of the source has been 'seen' to safely emit, not a longest-common-prefix agreement across repeated ASR hypotheses

Requires white-box access to the translating model's attention internals (offline alignment-head selection + runtime query/key capture) -- NOT reproducible against an API-only model like this repo's Gemini/OpenAI translator, where internal attention is inaccessible

Therefore this repo's h-localagreement-asr-commit should stay scoped to plain LocalAgreement-2 (agreement across consecutive Deepgram ASR hypotheses, both externally observable as text) rather than attempting an AlignAtt-style policy -- the reflections.md cycle-1 concern that AlignAtt4LLM's rule 'may differ from plain LocalAgreement-2 in a way that matters' is confirmed true, but the difference is a hard architectural blocker, not just a design nuance to account for

papers.title: Modeling and Improving Text Stability in Live Captions
papers.authors: Liu, Zhang, Du, et al. (Google Research)
papers.venue: ACM CHI 2023 (research.google blog post is a 2026-visible summary of the 2023 CHI paper, not a new 2026 paper)
papers.summary: Proposes a vision-based flicker metric -- luminance contrast + discrete Fourier transform applied to the *rendered* caption image, not a text/token diff -- to quantify what a viewer actually perceives as caption instability. Validated the metric against real viewer-reported distraction (moderate correlation, |r|~0.3) and introduced a stabilization algorithm (tokenized alignment + semantic merging + smooth animation) that a crowdsourced study (N=123) showed significantly reduces viewer distraction/fatigue and improves reading comfort.
key_findings: Vision-based (pixel/DFT) flicker measurement captures something text-based normalized erasure (NE) cannot: NE treats any token revision as equally bad, but a rendered-pixel metric would weight a revision by how visually jarring it actually is (position on screen, animation, font) -- NE is a reasonable cheap proxy but not a perceptual ground truth

The correlation with viewer experience is only moderate (~0.3), i.e. even a well-designed stability metric explains a minority of viewer-reported distraction -- a caution against over-indexing on any single flicker number (including this repo's own NE) as a proxy for caption quality

Out of scope for this repo right now: implementing this would require actually rendering captions to pixels and running DFT analysis, a much heavier lift than the retroactive text-level NE analysis already done in h-flicker-metric -- worth flagging as a possible future hypothesis (rendered-caption flicker) rather than pursuing this cycle

papers.title: NeMo@IWSLT 2026: Cascaded System for Simultaneous Speech Translation
papers.summary: NVIDIA's IWSLT 2026 submission cascades a dual-mode Unified ASR Transducer (trained to deliver stable transcriptions across a wide range of latencies) with a multilingual LLM for translation, covering En->De/It/Zh (standard and contextualized) and Cs->En. The key design choice is pushing stability into the ASR model itself via training, so the downstream LLM translation stage receives an already-stable source stream instead of needing its own stabilization logic.
key_findings: Confirms stability is being treated as a first-class training/architecture concern by 2026 SOTA cascade systems, not just a post-hoc metric -- validates this repo's decision (h-flicker-metric) to start measuring it at all

NeMo's approach (train the ASR model itself for cross-latency stability) is not retrofittable to this repo, which uses Deepgram as an off-the-shelf hosted ASR API with no training access -- this repo's realistic options remain post-hoc: masking (h-masking-holdback) or commit-gating (h-localagreement-asr-commit) applied to Deepgram's existing interim/final hypothesis stream

WebSearch could not surface NeMo's specific stability metric formula or numeric results (only the architecture-level design rationale) -- the full ACL Anthology paper (WebFetch to aclanthology.org is blocked in this environment, see note below) would be needed for a numeric comparison; not blocking any current hypothesis since NeMo's approach isn't applicable here anyway
